title: t-SNE & UMAP: Visualizing High-Dimensional Data
hook: t-SNE and UMAP squeeze thousands of dimensions into two so you can see whether your model's internal representations form meaningful clusters.
key_points: Both methods preserve local neighborhoods: points close in high dimensions land close in 2-D.
t-SNE minimizes KL divergence between pairwise similarity distributions; UMAP uses a graph-based approach.
UMAP is substantially faster than t-SNE and better at preserving global structure.
Output coordinates are not interpretable on their own - only relative positions matter.
Used heavily to visualize word embeddings, image features, and single-cell RNA-seq data.
content_html: t-SNE (t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding) and UMAP are nonlinear dimensionality reduction methods built for one purpose: making a 2-D scatter plot of data that originally lived in hundreds or thousands of dimensions, so you can see by eye whether similar things cluster together.
extra_html:
How it works

t-SNE, introduced by van der Maaten and Hinton in 2008, models pairwise similarities between points in the original space and in the 2-D space, then moves the 2-D points to make those similarity distributions match - using a Student t-distribution in the low-dimensional space to avoid crowding in the center. UMAP (McInnes et al., 2018) constructs a weighted graph of nearest neighbors in high dimensions and finds a low-dimensional layout that preserves that graph structure. It is generally faster than t-SNE and captures large-scale structure more faithfully.

Why it matters

These plots are how practitioners sanity-check representations: if a model has learned something meaningful, its internal embeddings should cluster by class or concept. Both t-SNE and UMAP are standard exploratory tools in NLP, computer vision, and genomics. Start with the original t-SNE paper by van der Maaten and Hinton, then read the UMAP paper for the improvements.

flashcards.prompt: What do both t-SNE and UMAP preserve when reducing to 2-D?
flashcards.back_html: Local neighborhoods: points close in high dimensions land close in the 2-D layout.

flashcards.prompt: How does UMAP compare to t-SNE?

choices.text: Substantially faster and better at preserving global structure
Slower but more accurate on local structure

flashcards.explanation_html: UMAP is substantially faster than t-SNE and better at preserving global structure.

flashcards.prompt: How should you interpret t-SNE/UMAP output coordinates?

choices.text: Only relative positions matter; the coordinates aren't interpretable alone
Each axis is a meaningful labeled feature
The absolute values give class probabilities

flashcards.explanation_html: The output coordinates are not interpretable on their own; only relative positions (whether things cluster) matter.
